Subject: Re: Out of office - Vacation message

Ward, Martin wrote:
> Just so as you know, a number of people/RBLs class OOO messages as spam.
> I believe that the logic is that if your mail server doesn't have a
> decent spam filter and if your OOO message includes a copy of the
> original email then a spammer can send rubbish to you and fake the From:
> address to be the person they really want it sent to. The spam can then
> be 'returned' to the person they want to receive it.
>
> Others consider these to be backscatter (see backscatterers.org, with
> whom I have already been in a length 'discussion' over what does and
> doesn't constitute spam).
>
> I personally think that there is a place for OOO messages, but it seems
> I am in a minority...
>   


should people drive without a license? should they drive while they are 
completely drunk?

The problem is not with ooo. the problem is with _broken_ ooo. If you 
don't have a "license", then you should not write an auto-responder.

if you write an automatic responder but you
- did not read RFC 3834
- don't have a good understanding of how smtp works
- don't understand the difference between envelope and recipient
then you are irresponsible.

now you can do whatever you want in your network, but don't blame the 
victims if you act irresponsibly.
